reader.notes: The receiver walk enters every occurrence through InitializeLoop, filters by Qualify's REPLACING arm and binds each store through MoveBinder.BindMoveOf, so the implicit MOVE is the explicit MOVE's code. Probe T13 (REPLACING NUMERIC on W-N(2:1) left unchanged) follows from a reference-modified item being alphanumeric.

refuter.evidence: Same repro as GR1 (rini3-001 at 85, rini3-002 at 2023): GR2b 'If identifier-1 references an elementary item, that item is initialized only if it belongs to the category specified in the REPLACING phrase' fails both ways for WA (2:1) of an alphabetic WA: not initialized under ALPHABETIC (M1[abc]), initialized under ALPHANUMERIC (M2[aQc]). cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.17.4 GR2 'that item is initialized only if it belongs to the category specified in the REPLACING phrase'; OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5. Everything else in the GR2 range probed and correct: rini2-001 every occurrence of a table with a subordinate REDEFINES D3[qq4qqq], REPLACING NUMERIC on a group holding a REDEFINES D7[qqqq] / on the redefining group D8[8qqq]; rini1-002 FILLER group's named items F3[Q0Q], REPLACING ALPHANUMERIC-EDITED / ALPHANUMERIC / NUMERIC-EDITED with editing and truncation E2, E3, E4. Cause site: InitializeBinder.cs#BindInitializeTarget RefModPlace arm.
refuter.corrected: Non-conforming (wrong-answer, cause b): with REPLACING, a reference-modified elementary identifier-1 is always judged alphanumeric, so the GR2b category test is wrong for an alphabetic data-name-1 (1985 ref-mod GR5 keeps it alphabetic).

adjudication.reason: INITIALIZE ... REPLACING treats a reference-modified alphabetic item as alphanumeric, so the wrong REPLACING phrase applies (`M2[aQc]` where `abc` is right). Both editions keep the item's category. Leads: the same "a reference-modified slice is always alphanumeric" assumption is written in `MoveOverlap.cs` and `ExpressionBinder.cs`, not probed.
